LESSON: READING 12.2. 1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 12 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we enjoy reading poems? 2. How are poems different from stories?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. adopt intensive reading in day-to-day communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication,

   Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression,

   Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension,

   Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. adopt intensive reading in day-to-day communication.

   Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a poem, song or passage that incorporates proverbs related to the theme and answer questions,

2. apply stress and rhythm

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a poem, song or passage that incorporates proverbs related to the theme and answer questions,
2. apply stress and rhythm

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner discusses and role plays with peers events in the passage or in the song.

• Self-efficacy: This is achieved as the learner answers questions from songs and poems, and takes part in the role play

confidently.

Values:
Responsibility: It is inculcated in the learner as they take upon assigned duties of reading the poems, discussing the events

and identifying the proverbs in the passage.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Online Safety: The learner’s knowledge on personal safety is emphasised when accessing internet resources to watch a

video on how people recite poems.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the skills acquired in reading intensively to their learning of reading skills in other areas such as

Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication,
2. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression,
3. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension,
4. adopt intensive reading in day-to-day communication.

Remember the key question: Why do we enjoy reading poems? 2. How are poems different from stories?
